claim: Atherosclerosis is a disease of chronic inflammation.
source: Atherosclerosis is a disease of chronic inflammation.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that represents established scientific understanding of atherosclerosis.

claim: IL-4 and IL-13 are the classical activators of STAT6.
source: We investigated the roles of the cytokines IL-4 and IL-13, the classical activators of STAT6, in the resolution of atherosclerosis inflammation.
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about STAT6 activation.

claim: Using Il4-/-Il13-/- mice, resolution was impaired.
source: Using Il4-/-Il13-/- mice, resolution was impaired
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1 showing no significant changes in plaque parameters after cholesterol lowering in Il4-/-Il13-/- mice.

claim: In both progressing and resolving plaques, levels of IL-4 were stably low and IL-13 was undetectable.
source: in both progressing and resolving plaques, levels of IL-4 were stably low and IL-13 was undetectable
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 3A where IL-4 levels were ~111-123 pg/mL and IL-13 was <3 pg/mL.

claim: IL-4 is required for atherosclerosis resolution, but collaborates with other factors.
source: This suggested that IL-4 is required for atherosclerosis resolution, but collaborates with other factors.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that IL-4 levels remain low and stable, yet resolution is impaired in Il4-/-Il13-/- mice.

claim: Increased Wnt signaling was observed in macrophages in resolving plaques.
source: We had observed increased Wnt signaling in macrophages in resolving plaques
evidence: This is supported by transcriptome data from laser-capture microdissected macrophages and scRNA-seq data presented in Figure 4.

claim: A loss-of-function Wnt mutation was associated with premature atherosclerosis in humans.
source: human genetic data from others showed that a loss-of-function Wnt mutation was associated with premature atherosclerosis
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by Mani et al., 2007.

claim: There is an inverse association between activation of Wnt signaling and disease severity in mice and humans.
source: We now find an inverse association between activation of Wnt signaling and disease severity in mice and humans.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4 showing Wnt gene expression patterns in mouse and human plaques, and Figure 6 showing impaired resolution with Wnt inhibition.

claim: Wnt enhanced the expression of inflammation resolving factors after treatment with plaque-relevant low concentrations of IL-4.
source: Wnt enhanced the expression of inflammation resolving factors after treatment with plaque-relevant low concentrations of IL-4.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro data in Figure 5 showing enhanced expression of Arg1, Ccl17, and Socs1 with Wnt3a+IL-4 treatment.

claim: Activation of the Wnt pathway following lipid lowering potentiates IL-4 responsiveness in macrophages via a PGE2/STAT3 axis.
source: Mechanistically, activation of the Wnt pathway following lipid lowering potentiates IL-4 responsiveness in macrophages via a PGE2/STAT3 axis.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 7 and 8 showing STAT3 activation by Wnt3a, PGE2 production, and requirement for both in enhanced IL-4 responses.

claim: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide according to the World Health Organization.
source: According to the World Health Organization, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is still the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide (WHO, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to WHO, 2017.

claim: Current therapies aim at inhibiting further progression of atherosclerosis, most commonly by lowering low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels.
source: Current therapies aim at inhibiting further progression of the disease, most commonly by lowering low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels.
evidence: This represents established clinical practice in cardiovascular medicine.

claim: The majority of treated patients will still undergo major coronary events according to several clinical trials.
source: Indeed, several clinical trials examining the effectiveness of available therapies concluded that the majority of treated patients will still undergo major coronary events (Libby, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Libby, 2005.

claim: Resolution of atherosclerosis has been demonstrated in several mouse models.
source: We and our collaborators have previously demonstrated a range of resolution of atherosclerosis in several mouse models (Rahman et al., 2017; Peled et al., 2017; Feig et al., 2011a; Chereshnev et al., 2003; Rahman and Fisher, 2018; Potteaux et al., 2011; Basu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Resolution entails a net decrease in plaque macrophage content, with the remaining macrophages showing a pro-resolving phenotype.
source: Collectively, our studies demonstrated that resolution entails a net decrease in plaque macrophage content, with the remaining macrophages showing a pro-resolving phenotype (Rahman and Fisher, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Rahman and Fisher, 2018.

claim: During disease progression, plaque macrophages are predominantly inflammatory, expressing factors such as CCL2, TNFα, and VCAM1.
source: For example, during disease progression, plaque macrophages are predominantly inflammatory, expressing factors such as C-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2) 1, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) ɑ, and vascular cell adhesion molecule (VCAM) 1 (Parathath et al., 2011; Cybulsky et al., 2001; Combadière et al., 2008; Boyle et al., 2003; Feig et al., 2011b).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: During resolution there is an accumulation of inflammation-resolving, tissue remodeling macrophages, which express ARG1 and MRC1.
source: Conversely, during resolution there is an accumulation of inflammation-resolving, tissue remodeling macrophages, which express arginase (ARG) 1 and mannose receptor (MRC) 1, and the concomitant loss of macrophages with the inflammatory subtype (Feig et al., 2011b; Hewing et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Feig et al., 2011b and Hewing et al., 2013.

claim: ARG1 has been previously considered to be a beneficial factor in atherosclerosis.
source: ARG1 has been previously considered to be a beneficial factor in atherosclerosis.
evidence: This represents established scientific understanding based on previous literature.

claim: Increased ARG1 activity would limit substrate to iNOS for conversion to damaging reactive nitrogen species.
source: A potential basis for this is that increased ARG1 activity would limit substrate to iNOS for conversion to damaging reactive nitrogen species (Munder, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Munder, 2009.

claim: ARG1 aids the licensing of macrophages to clear multiple apoptotic cells.
source: More recently, ARG1 was shown to aid the licensing of macrophages to clear multiple apoptotic cells, which would be expected to be important in atherosclerosis resolution (Yurdagul et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yurdagul et al., 2020.

claim: Arg1 expression is mainly regulated through STAT6.
source: Arg1 expression is mainly regulated through the canonical transcription factor for type 2 immune responses, signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) 6 (Van Dyken and Locksley, 2013; Rutschman et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Van Dyken and Locksley, 2013 and Rutschman et al., 2001.

claim: STAT6 is necessary for resolution of murine atherosclerosis.
source: Importantly, we recently showed that STAT6 is necessary for resolution of murine atherosclerosis in a process that also requires monocytes to be recruited to resolving plaques (Rahman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Rahman et al., 2017.

claim: Treatment with Pcsk9 AAV and WD caused a significant increase in total plasma cholesterol to ~500 mg/dL.
source: Treatment with the Pcsk9 AAV and WD caused a significant increase in total plasma cholesterol (~500 mg/dL)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: ApoB ASO injections decreased plasma cholesterol to normal levels (~60 mg/dL).
source: whereas subsequent ApoB ASO injections decreased plasma cholesterol to normal levels (~60 mg/dL, Figure 1B)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In WT mice, ApoB ASO administration for 3 weeks resulted in decreased plaque size and macrophage content in aortic roots.
source: We previously showed, in an identical experimental design, that ApoB ASO administration to Pcsk9 AAV and WD-treated WT mice for 3 weeks resulted in decreased plaque size and macrophage (CD68+ cells) content in aortic roots (Sharma et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sharma et al., 2020.

claim: Following cholesterol lowering, there were no significant changes in aortic root plaque size in Il4-/-Il13-/- mice.
source: In the present study, following cholesterol lowering, there were no significant changes in aortic root plaque size (Figure 1C)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Following cholesterol lowering, there were no significant changes in macrophage content in Il4-/-Il13-/- mice.
source: following cholesterol lowering, there were no significant changes in aortic root plaque size (Figure 1C), macrophage content (Figure 1D–F)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1D-F.

claim: Following cholesterol lowering, there were no significant changes in necrotic core area in Il4-/-Il13-/- mice.
source: following cholesterol lowering, there were no significant changes in aortic root plaque size (Figure 1C), macrophage content (Figure 1D–F), or necrotic core area (Figure 1G) in mice deficient in IL-4 and IL-13
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: IL-4/13 are needed for atherosclerosis resolution.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that IL-4/13 are needed for atherosclerosis resolution.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing impaired resolution in Il4-/-Il13-/- mice.

claim: Atherosclerosis resolution requires recruitment of new Stat6-expressing monocytes to plaques.
source: We previously reported that atherosclerosis resolution requires recruitment of new Stat6-expressing monocytes to plaques (Rahman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Rahman et al., 2017.

claim: The arch donors had elevated total cholesterol levels (978 ± 141 mg/dL).
source: As expected, the arch donors (and BL group) had elevated total cholesterol levels (978 ± 141 mg/dL)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The transplant recipients were normocholesterolemic (79 ± 22 mg/dL and 73 ± 10 mg/dL for WT and Il4-/-Il13-/- mice, respectively).
source: whereas the transplant recipients were normocholesterolemic (79 ± 22 mg/dL and 73 ± 10 mg/dL for WT and Il4-/-Il13-/- mice, respectively; Figure 2B)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There was a significant and comparable reduction (~60%) in plaque macrophages in both the WT and Il4-/-Il13-/- recipient groups.
source: there was a significant and comparable reduction (~60%) in plaque macrophages in both the WT and Il4-/-Il13-/- recipient groups (Figure 2D, E)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 2D and 2E.

claim: The necrotic core area significantly diminished in both recipient groups.
source: The necrotic core area significantly diminished as well in both recipient groups (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Resolution of atherosclerosis was similar in WT and Il4-/-Il13-/- recipients.
source: Thus, resolution of atherosclerosis was similar in WT and Il4-/-Il13-/- recipients (Figure 2D–G)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 2D-G.

claim: IL-4/13 production by cells newly recruited is not essential for resolution of atherosclerosis.
source: indicating that IL-4/13 production by cells newly recruited is not essential for resolution of atherosclerosis
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the aortic transplant data showing similar resolution in WT and Il4-/-Il13-/- recipients.

claim: The source of IL-4/13 needed for atherosclerosis resolution is from cells accumulating during the disease progression phase.
source: Our data thus far indicate that IL-4/13 are needed for atherosclerosis resolution, and the source of these cytokines is not from cells that are newly recruited in the resolution phase, but from cells accumulating during the disease progression phase.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined data of Figures 1 and 2.

claim: CCL2 abundance in plaques showed a marked decrease from progression to resolution.
source: Consistent with our previous reports (e.g., Rong et al., 2001), CCL2 abundance in plaques showed a marked decrease from progression to resolution (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and citation to Rong et al., 2001.

claim: IL-4 levels did not significantly change between progression (111 pg/mL) and resolution (123 pg/mL).
source: In contrast to CCL2, IL-4 levels did not significantly change between progression (111 pg/mL) and resolution (123 pg/mL; Figure 3A)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Plaque IL-4 levels were over two orders of magnitude lower than those commonly used in cell culture experiments (10–20 ng/mL).
source: and were strikingly lower (over two orders of magnitude) than those commonly used in cell culture experiments (10–20 ng/mL) (Minutti et al., 2017; Bosurgi et al., 2017; Sanin et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by comparison of measured plaque IL-4 levels with concentrations reported in cited literature.

claim: IL-13 was undetectable (<3 pg/mL) in both progressing and resolving plaques.
source: Interestingly, IL-13 was undetectable (<3 pg/mL) in both progressing and resolving plaques.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Only one cell in the entire dataset showed Il13 expression.
source: In accordance with the undetectable protein levels, only one cell in the entire dataset showed Il13 expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: ApoB ASO treatment led to reduction in plaque macrophages and promoted resolution of atherosclerosis.
source: We confirmed that ApoB ASO treatment led to reduction in plaque macrophages and promoted resolution of atherosclerosis (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: There was no significant difference in the proportion of IL-4-producing leukocytes when comparing mice from the BL (3.3%) and resolution (2.7%) groups.
source: Results showed no significant difference in the proportion of IL-4-producing leukocytes (CD45+ cells) when comparing mice from the BL (3.3%) and resolution (2.7%) groups (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Small amounts of IL-4-producing cells accumulate in progressing plaques and do not increase further during the resolution phase.
source: Our data suggest that small amounts of IL-4-producing cells accumulate in progressing plaques and do not increase further during the resolution phase.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the flow cytometry data in Figure 3E.

claim: In the reparative environment, the IL-4 that accumulated is apparently sufficient to activate STAT6, which in turn polarizes plaque macrophages to pro-resolving cells.
source: In the reparative environment, the IL-4 that accumulated is apparently sufficient to activate STAT6, which in turn polarizes plaque macrophages to pro-resolving cells.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data combining observations about IL-4 levels and STAT6 requirement.

claim: Transcriptome data from macrophages from progressing and resolving plaques suggested activation of the Wnt pathway.
source: To explore this, we reviewed our transcriptome data from macrophages taken by laser-capture microdissection from progressing and resolving plaques (Ramsey et al., 2014). These data (from two independent mouse models (Feig et al., 2011a) suggested activation of the Wnt pathway (Ramsey et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ramsey et al., 2014 and Feig et al., 2011a.

claim: A mutation causing downregulation of the Wnt pathway led to early coronary artery disease in humans.
source: This was of particular interest since a mutation causing downregulation of this pathway led to early coronary artery disease in humans (Mani et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mani et al., 2007.

claim: Activation of Wnt signaling in macrophages inhibits atherosclerosis progression.
source: Moreover, activation of Wnt signaling in macrophages was recently shown to inhibit atherosclerosis progression (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2018.

claim: In disease resolution there is an overall increase in the expression of Wnt-related genes across most clusters.
source: Notably, comparison between progressing and resolving plaque macrophages demonstrated that in disease resolution there is an overall increase in the expression of Wnt-related genes across most clusters (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Cttnb1, the gene encoding for β-catenin, was the most upregulated across macrophage clusters.
source: Among the Wnt regulated genes, Cttnb1, the gene encoding for β-catenin, the downstream canonical effector of Wnt, was the most upregulated across macrophage clusters (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Seven out of 10 Wnt-responsive genes had lower expression levels in symptomatic patients' plaque macrophages compared to asymptomatic patients.
source: Results show that of the 10 genes 7 had lower expression levels in Sym patients' plaque macrophages compared to Asym patients (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of human endarterectomy data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: A permutation test resulted in a p-value=0.008, supporting an inverse relationship between Wnt signaling and disease severity across species.
source: A permutation test resulted in a p-value=0.008, thereby supporting a bona fide inverse relationship between Wnt signaling and disease severity across species, consistent with the genetic loss-of-function association with premature CAD (coronary artery disease; Mani et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the data in Figure 4D and citation to Mani et al., 2007.

claim: Wnt scores at the 3-month follow-up were significantly increased relative to disease presentation.
source: The fold-change of each gene expression at the follow-up compared to presentation was calculated per patient and summed to create a 'Wnt score'. These scores at the 3-month follow-up were significantly increased relative to disease presentation, indicated by the increased Wnt score (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of human PBMC data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The expression of Axin2 significantly correlated with a decrease in plaque volume (R2 = 0.408, p=0.002).
source: Notably, the expression of Axin2, the hallmark Wnt target gene (Jho et al., 2002; Lustig et al., 2002), significantly correlated with a decrease in plaque volume (R2 = 0.408, p=0.002; Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4F and citations to Jho et al., 2002 and Lustig et al., 2002.

claim: Treatment with Wnt3a activated the Wnt pathway, indicated by the upregulation of Axin2.
source: First, we confirmed that treatment with Wnt3a activated the Wnt pathway, indicated by the upregulation of Axin2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Treatment with Wnt3a resulted in accumulation of β-catenin.
source: First, we confirmed that treatment with Wnt3a activated the Wnt pathway, indicated by the upregulation of Axin2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) and the accumulation of the transcription co-activator β-catenin (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Wnt3a treatment did not alter the expression of pro-resolution genes (Arg1, Ccl17, and Socs1).
source: Examination of genes associated with pro-resolution (e.g., Arg1, Ccl17, and Socs1) revealed that Wnt3a treatment did not alter their expression.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: When cells were co-treated with Wnt3a and IL-4, pro-resolution transcripts showed increased expression relative to IL-4 alone.
source: However, when cells were co-treated with Wnt3a and IL-4, these transcripts showed increased expression relative to IL-4 alone (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figures 5A-C.

claim: The enhanced expression of pro-resolving genes is not due to Wnt3a-induced production of IL-4/13.
source: To examine whether the enhanced expression of these pro-resolving genes is due to Wnt3a-induced production of IL-4/13, we repeated the in vitro experiments with Il4-/-Il13-/- BMDMs. The data show that the expression of the pro-resolving genes was enhanced in cells co-treated with Wnt3a and IL-4 (Figure 5D–F), indicating that the increased gene expression cannot be explained by induced production of IL-4/13.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from Il4-/-Il13-/- BMDMs shown in Figures 5D-F.

claim: Stat6 deficiency completely abrogated the expression of Arg1, Ccl17, and Socs1 and the enhancement observed in cells co-treated with Wnt3a and IL-4.
source: As shown in Figure 5G–I, Stat6 deficiency completely abrogated the expression of Arg1, Ccl17, and Socs1 and the enhancement observed in cells co-treated with Wnt3a and IL-4.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from Stat6-/- BMDMs shown in Figures 5G-I.

claim: Wnt signaling cooperates with IL-4/STAT6 signaling to augment macrophage pro-resolving gene expression.
source: In sum, the data suggest that Wnt signaling cooperates with IL-4/STAT6 signaling to augment macrophage pro-resolving gene expression.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined data in Figure 5.

claim: Mice treated with LGK974 had similar body weights compared to the control group.
source: Mice treated with LGK974 had similar body weights (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Mice treated with LGK974 had similar lipid profiles compared to the control group.
source: Mice treated with LGK974 had similar body weights (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), lipid profiles (Figure 6B)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Mice treated with LGK974 had similar hematological parameters compared to the control group.
source: Mice treated with LGK974 had similar body weights (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), lipid profiles (Figure 6B), hematological parameters (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–E)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 6—figure supplement 1B-E.

claim: Mice treated with LGK974 had similar frequencies of Ly6Chi and Ly6Clo circulating monocytes compared to the control group.
source: Mice treated with LGK974 had similar body weights (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), lipid profiles (Figure 6B), hematological parameters (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–E), and frequencies of Ly6Chi and Ly6Clo circulating monocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F) compared to the control (Ctrl) group.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Plaques from LGK974-treated mice showed significantly less active β-catenin.
source: To confirm that Wnt inhibition was successful in the LGK974-treated mice, plaques were stained for the active form of β-catenin (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G), which showed significantly less active β-catenin.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1G.

claim: LGK974 treatment decreased expression of Lef1 and Axin2 in plaque macrophages.
source: To verify that LGK974 treatment inhibited Wnt signaling in plaque macrophages, we excised them using laser capture microdissection (LCM) and examined the expression of Wnt-responsive genes. The data show decreased expression of Lef1 and Axin2 from LGK974 compared to vehicle-treated mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from LCM-excised macrophages shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Plaque area and macrophage content were significantly decreased in the control group compared to BL.
source: Plaque area and macrophage content were significantly decreased in the control group compared to BL (Figure 6C–F).
evidence: This is supported by morphometric data shown in Figures 6C-F.

claim: Mice that received the Wnt inhibitor did not have a significant decrease in plaque or macrophage area.
source: However, mice that received the Wnt inhibitor did not have a significant decrease in plaque or macrophage area (Figure 6C–F), despite equally low cholesterol levels (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by morphometric data shown in Figures 6C-F and cholesterol data in Figure 6B.

claim: Resolving plaques are enriched with collagen, presumably because the content of matrix metalloprotease-producing macrophages decline.
source: Furthermore, we previously reported that resolving plaques are enriched with collagen, presumably because the content of matrix metalloprotease-producing macrophages decline (Peled et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Peled et al., 2017.

claim: An increase in plaque collagen was observed in the control resolution group, but not in the Wnt inhibitor group.
source: We again observed this increase in plaque collagen in the control resolution group, but it was not detected in the Wnt inhibitor group (Figure 6F, G).
evidence: This is supported by collagen staining data shown in Figures 6F and 6G.

claim: In control resolution there was downregulation of the pro-inflammatory markers CCL2 and VCAM1, which were not attenuated in the LGK974 group.
source: Consistent with this, plaque immunostaining showed that in control resolution there was downregulation of the pro-inflammatory markers CCL2 and VCAM1, which were not attenuated in the LGK974 group.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 6F and 6G.

claim: Compared to BL mice, in the control group there were increases in pro-resolving markers ARG1 and MRC1, which were not seen in the LGK974 group.
source: Additionally, compared to BL mice, in the control group there were increases in pro-resolving markers ARG1 and MRC1, which were not seen in the LGK974 group (Figure 6F, G).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 6F and 6G.

claim: Wnt inhibition impairs atherosclerosis resolution and results in decreased accumulation of pro-resolving plaque macrophages.
source: Overall, these data suggest that Wnt inhibition impairs atherosclerosis resolution and results in decreased accumulation of pro-resolving plaque macrophages.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined data in Figure 6.

claim: The untreated BMDMs cluster with the IL-4-treated cells in PCA analysis.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) shows that the untreated BMDMs cluster with the IL-4-treated cells (Figure 7A), indicating a high similarity of transcriptional profiles (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A) before Wnt-mediated augmentation.
evidence: This is supported by PCA analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Wnt3a-treated (−/+ IL-4) cells clustered together and were distinct from the control and IL-4-treated cells.
source: Wnt3a-treated (−/+ IL-4) cells clustered together were distinct from the control and IL-4-treated cells (Figure 7A) and exhibited extensive transcriptional changes (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by PCA analysis shown in Figure 7A and differential expression analysis in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Both Wnt3a and Wnt3a+IL-4-treated cells had the KEGG pathway term 'JAK-STAT signaling pathway' in the top seven most significantly enriched pathways.
source: The data suggested a possible engagement of the JAK-STAT pathway in Wnt3a-treated cells as both Wnt3a and Wnt3a+IL-4-treated cells had the KEGG pathway term 'JAK-STAT signaling pathway' in the top seven most significantly enriched pathways (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: IL-6 and IL-10 collaborate with IL-4 to enhance Arg1 expression in macrophages.
source: Moreover, the STAT3 activating cytokines IL-6 and IL-10 have been reported to collaborate with IL-4 to enhance Arg1 expression in macrophages (Makita et al., 2015; Mauer et al., 2014), as we also found (Figure 7B, C).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Makita et al., 2015 and Mauer et al., 2014, and data shown in Figures 7B and 7C.

claim: STAT3 is phosphorylated after 16 hr of Wnt3a treatment.
source: The data show that STAT3 is not phosphorylated after a short exposure to Wnt3a (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C); however, after 16 hr of treatment, there was substantial STAT3 phosphorylation (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The STAT3 target gene Socs3 was upregulated following Wnt3a treatment.
source: Furthermore, the STAT3 target gene Socs3 was upregulated following Wnt3a treatment (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Stat3 knockdown attenuated Arg1 expression in response to Wnt3a+IL-4.
source: Results show that Stat3 KD attenuated Arg1 expression in response to Wnt3a+IL-4 (Figure 7F), suggesting that STAT3 is required for the enhancement of IL-4 responses by Wnt3a.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from Stat3 siRNA-treated cells shown in Figure 7F.

claim: There was less nuclear STAT3 localization in plaques of mice treated with LGK974 compared to the control group.
source: To explore whether Wnt inhibition affects STAT3 activity in vivo, aortic root sections from control and LGK974-treated mice (Figure 6A) were stained for STAT3, and its nuclear localization was determined. Images and their analyses show less nuclear STAT3 localization in plaques of mice treated with LGK974 compared to the control group (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: Wnt enhances the response to IL-4 via STAT3 activation.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that Wnt enhances the response to IL-4 via STAT3 activation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined data in Figure 7.

claim: Wnt CM caused STAT3 phosphorylation after 15 min, while Wnt3a itself failed to do so.
source: The data show that the CM caused STAT3 phosphorylation after 15 min, while Wnt3a itself failed to do so (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Co-treatment of BMDMs with Wnt3a, as well as Wnt CM, in combination with IL-4 promoted enhanced Arg1 expression compared with IL-4-only treatment.
source: Similar to our previous results, co-treatment of BMDMs with Wnt3a, as well as Wnt CM, in combination with IL-4 promoted enhanced Arg1 expression compared with IL-4-only treatment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Wnt CM retained its IL-4 augmentation ability after treatment with a Wnt3a-blocking antibody.
source: To confirm that the augmentation in Arg1 expression is not due to residual Wnt3a, CM was treated with a Wnt3a-blocking antibody prior to its exposure to naïve BMDMs. The data show that the CM retained its IL-4 augmentation ability (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F), suggesting that Wnt3a stimulated the production and/or secretion of a factor/s other than itself that, in turn, activated STAT3.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Blocking TGFβ, CXCR3, gp130, IL10R, or HGFR did not attenuate Arg1 expression in Wnt3a+IL-4-treated cells.
source: Arg1 expression was not attenuated by blocking any of the aforementioned proteins in Wnt3a+IL-4-treated cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1G), indicating that these factors do not play a role in the enhanced pro-resolving gene expression following Wnt3a treatment.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Several lipid mediators were upregulated in CM of Wnt3a-treated BMDMs.
source: We found that several lipid mediators were upregulated in CM of Wnt3a-treated BMDMs (Figure 8A), notably at the time when CM enhances the response to IL-4.
evidence: This is supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: There was a global increase of arachidonic acid metabolites, such as TXB2, PGE2, PGD2, PGF2a, peaking 16 hr post-Wnt3a treatment.
source: Specifically, there was a global increase of arachidonic acid metabolites, such as TXB2, PGE2, PGD2, PGF2a, peaking 16 hr post-Wnt3a treatment (respective fold changes of 18, 58, 101, and 5, Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: There is a high degree of correlation in gene expression between BMDMs treated with Wnt3a+IL-4 and PGE2+IL-4, with r2 = 0.481 and p-value<2.34−75.
source: Thus, we compared those data to our RNA-seq data of BMDMs co-treated with Wnt3a and IL-4. The data show a high degree of correlation in gene expression between BMDMs treated with Wnt3a+IL-4 and PGE2+IL-4, with r2 = 0.481 and p-value<2.34−75 (Figure 8B), despite marked differences in the IL-4 concentrations used in these experiments (0.1 and 20 ng/mL, Sanin et al., 2018, respectively).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 8B comparing data from this study with Sanin et al., 2018.

claim: Wnt3a treatment increased Ptgs2 expression in BMDMs.
source: Because the canonical Wnt pathway was previously shown (e.g., Araki et al., 2003; Nunez et al., 2011) to regulate Ptgs2 expression (the enzyme that metabolizes arachidonic acid to PGH2, the PGE2 precursor), we examined its levels following Wnt3a stimulation in BMDMs. The results show increased Ptgs2 expression upon Wnt3a treatment
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8C and citations to Araki et al., 2003 and Nunez et al., 2011.

claim: Wnt3a treatment increased Ptges expression in BMDMs.
source: The results show increased Ptgs2 expression upon Wnt3a treatment, as well as upregulation of the next enzyme in the PGE2 production pathway, Ptges (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Wnt3a decreased the expression of Hpgd.
source: In addition to the increase in these enzymes that produce PGE2, Wnt3a also decreased the expression of Hpgd, which inactivates PGE2 and serves as a negative regulator of its levels (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: PGE2 blockade completely abrogated the enhancement in gene expression by Wnt CM.
source: First, Wnt CM was treated with a PGE2-blocking antibody and then added to naive BMDMs together with IL-4 for 2.5 hr. While blocking of Wnt3a itself in Wnt CM did not alter the augmented Arg1 expression (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F), PGE2 blockade completely abrogated the enhancement in gene expression (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: BMDMs in which both EP2 and EP4 receptors were inhibited simultaneously did not show enhanced Arg1 expression upon Wnt3a+IL-4 or CM+IL-4 treatment.
source: However, BMDMs in which both receptors were inhibited simultaneously did not show enhanced Arg1 expression upon Wnt3a+IL-4 or CM+IL-4 treatment, but rather responded similarly to IL-4-only-treated cells (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The expression of Ptges was reduced by 58% in the LGK974 group compared to controls.
source: Although expression of Ptgs2 and Hpgd did not differ between the two groups, the expression of Ptges was reduced by 58% in the LGK974 group compared to controls (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from LCM-excised macrophages shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Macrophages activated by the Wnt pathway produce and secrete PGE2, activating STAT3 in an autocrine/paracrine fashion, which subsequently cooperates with IL-4/STAT6.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that macrophages activated by the Wnt pathway produce and secrete PGE2, activating STAT3 in an autocrine/paracrine fashion, which subsequently cooperates with IL-4/STAT6 (Figure 8G).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined data in Figure 8.

claim: In atherosclerosis, the Wnt/PGE2/STAT3 mechanism primes the response of plaque macrophages to IL-4 that accumulates in plaques during disease progression and together induce resolution of atherosclerosis.
source: In atherosclerosis, this mechanism primes the response of plaque macrophages to IL-4 that accumulates in plaques during disease progression and together induce resolution of atherosclerosis.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation integrating all the findings into a model for atherosclerosis resolution.

claim: ARG1 is essential for the clearance of multiple apoptotic cells.
source: Among these is Arg1, which, besides depriving substrate to damaging iNOS (Munder, 2009), has been recently shown to be essential for the clearance of multiple apoptotic cells (Yurdagul et al., 2020), an important process in inflammation resolution in plaques and in general (Libby et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yurdagul et al., 2020 and Libby et al., 2014.

claim: IL-4 alone is not sufficient for atherosclerosis resolution.
source: These results suggest that IL-4 alone is not sufficient for atherosclerosis resolution and that Wnt signaling cooperates with IL-4 to enhance its induction of the expression of genes associated with inflammation resolution.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined experimental findings.

claim: The inability of IL-4/13 to independently mount a sufficient response in macrophages to promote tissue repair has been shown in other contexts, including in the lungs after helminth infection or in the gut after induction of colitis.
source: Of note, the inability of IL-4/13 to independently mount a sufficient response in macrophages to promote tissue repair, which atherosclerosis is an example of, has been recently shown in other contexts, including in the lungs after helminth infection or in the gut after induction of colitis (Bosurgi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bosurgi et al., 2017.

claim: Recognition of apoptotic cells through MerTK and Axl together with IL-4 was needed for induction of tissue repair in lung and gut models.
source: Rather, recognition of apoptotic cells through the receptors MER proto-oncogene, tyrosine kinase (MerTK) and Axl receptor tyrosine kinase together with IL-4 was needed for this induction in these two models (Bosurgi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bosurgi et al., 2017.

claim: IL-4/13 collaborate with local tissue enhancers that amplify their response upon helminth infection.
source: Another relevant study showed that IL-4/13 collaborate with local tissue enhancers that amplify their response upon helminth infection (Minutti et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Minutti et al., 2017.

claim: Deletion of local tissue enhancers caused a drastic impairment in the inflammatory response against parasites, although IL-4/13 levels were unaffected.
source: Deletion of these local enhancers caused a drastic impairment in the inflammatory response against parasites, although IL-4/13 levels were unaffected.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Minutti et al., 2017.

claim: The need for tissue enhancers arises from relatively low tissue IL-4 concentrations.
source: It is plausible that the need for tissue enhancers arises from relatively low tissue IL-4 concentrations, which is supported by our finding that plaques contain ~100 pg/mL IL-4 (Figure 3A), a concentration that is 100–200-fold lower than what is used in typical in vitro studies (e.g., Minutti et al., 2017; Bosurgi et al., 2017; Sanin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by the measured IL-4 concentrations and comparison with literature.

claim: Wnt3a caused the activation of STAT3 and enhanced IL-4 responses in a model of kidney injury and fibrosis.
source: This is in accordance with the aforementioned report showing enhanced response of BMDMs to IL-4 following Wnt3a treatment via activation of STAT3 in a model of kidney injury (Feng et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Feng et al., 2018.

claim: STAT3 and STAT6 cooperate to increase Arg1 gene expression.
source: as well as with the suggestion that STAT3 and STAT6 cooperate to increase Arg1 gene expression (reviewed in Pourcet and Pineda-Torra, 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pourcet and Pineda-Torra, 2013.

claim: STAT3 (activated by IL-6) and STAT6 (activated by IL-4) cooperate to enhance expression and secretion of cathepsins, to promote polarization of tumor-associated macrophages.
source: For instance, it had been previously shown that STAT3 (activated by IL-6) and STAT6 (activated by IL-4) cooperate to enhance expression and secretion of cathepsins, to promote polarization of tumor-associated macrophages (Yan et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yan et al., 2016.

claim: STAT3 and STAT6 cooperate to enhance IL-4-induced gene expression.
source: STAT3 (activated by IL-6) and STAT6 (activated by IL-4) cooperate to enhance expression and secretion of cathepsins, to promote polarization of tumor-associated macrophages (Yan et al., 2016) and enhance IL-4-induced gene expression (Makita et al., 2015; Fernando et al., 2014; Figure 7B, C).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Makita et al., 2015 and Fernando et al., 2014, and data in Figures 7B and 7C.

claim: PGE2 promotes the phosphorylation of STAT3 in various cell types.
source: Our data further suggest that STAT3 is activated following Wnt stimulation via PGE2 since the latter is produced by Wnt3a-treated BMDMs (Figure 8A) and has been shown to promote the phosphorylation of STAT3 in various cell types (Jw et al., 2019; Chun et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2015; Halpern et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jw et al., 2019; Chun et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2015; and Halpern et al., 2019.

claim: Wnt signaling promotes the production of PGE2 through transcriptional regulation of Ptgs2.
source: Wnt signaling promotes the production of PGE2 through transcriptional regulation of Ptgs2 (Araki et al., 2003; Nunez et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Araki et al., 2003 and Nunez et al., 2011.

claim: PGE2 amplifies IL-4-induced gene expression in macrophages.
source: PGE2 itself was previously shown to amplify IL-4-induced gene expression in macrophages (Sanin et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2016; Luan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sanin et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2016; and Luan et al., 2015.

claim: Inhibition of PGE2 responses via deletion of EP4 decreased early atherosclerosis burden.
source: Initially, it was reported that inhibition of PGE2 responses via deletion of its receptor EP4 (but not EP2) decreased early atherosclerosis burden (Babaev et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Babaev et al., 2008.

claim: EP4 deficiency in bone marrow or myeloid cells caused an increase in plaque inflammation and macrophage content.
source: Later reports showed that EP4 deficiency in bone marrow (Tang et al., 2011) or myeloid cells (Vallerie et al., 2016) caused an increase in plaque inflammation and macrophage content, without affecting diabetic atherosclerosis.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tang et al., 2011 and Vallerie et al., 2016.

claim: Engagement of the PGE2 receptor EP4 in macrophages may be beneficial for dampening atherosclerosis progression and enhancing disease resolution.
source: These data, together with results presented here, indicate that engagement of the PGE2 receptor EP4 in macrophages may be beneficial not only for dampening atherosclerosis progression, but also enhancing disease resolution.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined literature and experimental data.

claim: Whether direct activation of the receptors for PGE2 will enhance atherosclerosis resolution merits additional investigation.
source: However, whether direct activation of the receptors for PGE2 will enhance atherosclerosis resolution merits additional investigation.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: The human data suggest a systemic increase in Wnt responsiveness since circulating immune cells showed higher expression of Wnt-responsive genes in patients whose plaques were regressing.
source: Notably, there was a marked decrease in macrophage content of both WT and Il4-/- arch recipients (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E, G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-E, G.
